CSIM safeguarding policy covering prevention of sexual exploitation, abuse and harassment (PSEA / SEA-H). Compliant with EU SEA-H self-evaluation questionnaire and CHS standards.

output.executive_summary:
CSIM (Center for Syrian Independent Media), a Syrian-led nonprofit media-development consortium registered in Türkiye and operating across Syria, is exceptionally well-positioned to lead a grant action under Lot 3 (Promotion of and support to media freedom and pluralism in Syria) of EuropeAid/185831/DD/ACT/SY. Since its founding in 2018, CSIM has built a distinctive operational footprint spanning Istanbul, Gaziantep, Erbil, and Qamishli, with a vetted network of Syrian journalists and newsrooms operating in Arabic and Kurdish across multiple Syrian governorates. The organisation has delivered four sub-million-EUR grants on time and without audit qualification, holds a clean KPMG Türkiye audit for 2024, and has worked under SIDA, Free Press Unlimited, and Internews frameworks — demonstrating the financial management maturity and donor-compliance culture the European Commission requires.

CSIM's three core win-themes align directly with the three Lot 3 priorities. First, CSIM's established journalism training and protection programming directly addresses Priority 1 (strengthening independent media and journalists to exercise fundamental freedoms) and Priority 2 (effective protection of and support to journalists, bloggers, and other media workers), backed by a documented safeguarding policy and a field presence inside Syria. Second, CSIM's multi-platform Arabic and Kurdish content production and information-integrity programming position it to deliver Priority 3 (strengthened public awareness and inclusive debate on the centrality of media freedom) at scale and in the languages of the target population. Third, CSIM's Syrian-led identity and cross-border operational model — combining diaspora editorial coaching with in-country field nodes — offers the EU a partner that is simultaneously embedded in Syrian civil society and capable of meeting international accountability standards.

The fixed grant ceiling for Lot 3 is EUR 675,000, with a co-financing floor of 10% (90% EU co-financing permitted for applicants not established in Syria; 100% for lead applicants established in eligible locations under Section 2.1.3). CSIM should clarify its eligibility for the 100% co-financing rate given its Türkiye registration. The organisation must complete PADOR registration before the 18 May 2026 submission deadline, and should identify an EU-eligible co-applicant to strengthen the consortium's geographic and thematic coverage. With these administrative steps resolved, CSIM presents a compelling, evidence-backed candidacy for Lot 3.
technical_approach: Context Analysis and Needs Assessment. Syria's post-Assad transitional environment presents acute and compounding threats to media freedom. Fourteen years of conflict have decimated independent newsrooms, normalised self-censorship, and left journalists — particularly women, Kurdish-language reporters, and those operating in contested governorates — without legal protection, digital security tools, or sustainable income. CSIM's field nodes in Gaziantep, Erbil, and Qamishli, combined with its Istanbul editorial hub, provide a living context-intelligence system. At project inception, CSIM will conduct a structured needs assessment across at least four Syrian governorates, using key-informant interviews with active journalists, focus groups with community media audiences, and a desk review of existing media-freedom monitoring data (RSF, CPJ, Syria Media Forum). The assessment will map: (a) the number and profile of active independent media outlets and freelance journalists; (b) the nature and frequency of threats (physical, legal, digital, economic); (c) existing capacity gaps in editorial standards, digital security, and business sustainability; and (d) audience information needs and trust levels. Findings will be validated with the co-applicant partner and shared with the EU Delegation before activity design is finalised, ensuring the intervention logic is grounded in verified evidence rather than assumption.

Intervention Logic and Theory of Change. CSIM's theory of change holds that sustainable media freedom in Syria requires simultaneous investment in three mutually reinforcing domains: journalist capability, journalist protection, and public demand for independent media. Without capability, journalists cannot produce credible content; without protection, they cannot operate safely; without public demand, independent outlets cannot survive commercially or politically. The action's results chain is structured accordingly. Inputs (EU grant funds, CSIM staff expertise, co-applicant networks, field infrastructure) will finance Activities (training cohorts, protection-response mechanisms, public-awareness campaigns) that generate Outputs (number of journalists trained, protection cases managed, media-literacy sessions delivered, content pieces produced). Outputs will accumulate into Outcomes (improved editorial quality and safety practices among target journalists; increased public recognition of media freedom as a civic right) that contribute to the Impact (a more pluralistic, independent, and resilient Syrian media ecosystem that supports democratic transition). Each result level will carry SMART indicators, baselines established in the inception phase, and targets verified through quarterly monitoring.

Priority 1 — Strengthening Independent Media and Journalists. CSIM will deliver a structured capacity-development programme targeting 60 Syrian journalists and 12 newsroom editors across Arabic- and Kurdish-language outlets operating inside Syria and in diaspora hubs. The programme will comprise: (a) a modular journalism-skills curriculum covering investigative reporting, fact-checking, editorial ethics, and audience engagement, delivered in Arabic and Kurdish through a blended in-person and online format; (b) one-to-one editorial coaching for newsroom editors, drawing on CSIM's established coaching methodology for Syrian newsrooms in exile; and (c) a peer-learning network connecting trained journalists across governorates to sustain knowledge transfer beyond the grant period. Training content will be contextualised to Syria's transitional political environment, including modules on reporting on transitional justice, covering displaced communities, and navigating relationships with new authorities. All training materials will be made openly available in Arabic and Kurdish under a Creative Commons licence to maximise reach and sustainability.

Priority 2 — Protection of Journalists, Bloggers, and Media Workers. CSIM will operationalise a Journalist Protection Mechanism (JPM) building on its existing safeguarding policy framework. The JPM will provide: (a) a rapid-response legal and psychosocial support pathway for journalists facing threats, detention, or harassment, coordinated with the co-applicant's legal network; (b) digital-security training and tool provision (VPN, encrypted communications, secure device protocols) for at least 80 media workers, with priority given to women journalists and those operating in high-risk governorates; (c) a threat-monitoring and documentation function, producing quarterly public reports on journalist safety incidents in Syria, contributing to the global evidence base maintained by RSF and CPJ; and (d) a small emergency-assistance fund (subject to EU approval of financial-support-to-third-parties modality) to cover immediate relocation or legal costs for journalists at acute risk. The JPM will be governed by a Protection Committee comprising CSIM's safeguarding lead, the co-applicant's legal officer, and an independent Syrian civil-society representative, meeting monthly to review cases and escalate as needed.

Priority 3 — Public Awareness and Inclusive Debate on Media Freedom. CSIM will design and implement a multi-platform media-freedom awareness campaign targeting Syrian audiences inside the country and in diaspora communities. The campaign will produce: (a) a series of 24 short-form documentary and explainer videos in Arabic and Kurdish, distributed via YouTube, Telegram, and partner broadcast outlets, covering topics such as the right to information, how to identify disinformation, and the role of independent media in democratic transition; (b) six community dialogue events in partnership with local civil-society organisations in Qamishli, Gaziantep, and at least two additional locations, bringing together journalists, community leaders, youth groups, and women's organisations to discuss media freedom as a civic issue; and (c) a media-literacy toolkit for secondary schools and community centres, developed with input from educators and youth representatives, and piloted in at least three locations. All campaign materials will integrate gender-sensitive messaging and will be accessible to persons with disabilities (audio-described video, large-print text versions).

Cross-Cutting Issues Integration. Gender equality will be mainstreamed throughout the action: at least 40% of training beneficiaries will be women journalists; the JPM will include a gender-sensitive threat-assessment protocol; and campaign content will explicitly address the specific risks faced by women media workers. Minority rights will be addressed through the Kurdish-language strand of all activities and through dedicated outreach to Syriac, Armenian, and other minority-community media. Youth will be prioritised in the media-literacy campaign and through a junior-journalist mentorship track within the capacity-development programme. Disability inclusion will be addressed through accessible event formats and accessible digital content. Environmental considerations will be integrated by minimising travel through hybrid delivery models and by including environmental reporting as a journalism-skills module topic. CSIM will appoint a cross-cutting issues focal point responsible for monitoring integration across all workstreams and reporting on it in quarterly narrative reports.

Partnership and Co-Applicant Rationale. CSIM intends to identify and formalise a partnership with one EU-eligible co-applicant organisation with complementary expertise, preferably a European press-freedom or media-development organisation with established EU grant management experience and a legal network relevant to journalist protection. The co-applicant will contribute: EU grant management capacity (strengthening the consortium's administrative compliance profile); legal expertise for the JPM; and access to European advocacy networks for the media-freedom awareness component. The division of responsibilities will be formalised in a partnership agreement prior to submission, with CSIM as lead applicant retaining overall programmatic and financial accountability. The co-applicant selection process will be completed by March 2026 to allow adequate time for joint concept-note drafting and PADOR verification.

Monitoring, Evaluation, and Learning. CSIM will implement a results-based monitoring framework aligned with the EU's intervention-logic requirements. A baseline survey will be conducted in month one; mid-term review in month twelve; and final evaluation in month twenty-four (or at project end). Key performance indicators will include: number of journalists trained (disaggregated by gender, language, and governorate); number of protection cases managed and resolved; number of media-freedom awareness campaign views and community dialogue participants; and a media-freedom perception index measured through audience surveys at baseline and endline. CSIM's project director will hold overall M&E responsibility, supported by a dedicated M&E officer. Quarterly progress reports and financial reports will be submitted to the EU Delegation in the format prescribed by the grant contract. CSIM's KPMG Türkiye audit relationship will be maintained throughout the project to ensure annual financial audits meet EU standards. A learning review will be conducted at project close to document lessons for the Syrian media-development sector.

output.cover_letter_draft:
18 March 2026

To the Evaluation Committee,
European Commission — EU Delegation to Syria
Call for Proposals EuropeAid/185831/DD/ACT/SY
Support to Justice, Freedom of Expression and Social Cohesion in Syria — Lot 3

Dear Members of the Evaluation Committee,

On behalf of the Center for Syrian Independent Media (CSIM), I am pleased to submit this concept note in response to Lot 3 (Promotion of and support to media freedom and pluralism in Syria) of the above-referenced call for proposals. CSIM is a Syrian-led nonprofit media-development consortium, registered in Türkiye and operating across Syria since 2018, with field nodes in Gaziantep, Erbil, and Qamishli and an editorial hub in Istanbul. Our mission is to strengthen independent Syrian journalism and protect the journalists who practise it — a mission that aligns precisely with the three priorities of Lot 3 and with the European Commission's broader objective of contributing to sustainable, rights-based development in Syria during this critical transitional period. We believe that a free, pluralistic, and professional Syrian media sector is not a peripheral concern but a foundational condition for the inclusive democratic transition that the EU and the Syrian people are working to build together.

CSIM brings to this action a combination of assets that is rare among organisations working on Syrian media freedom. We have delivered four grants totalling under EUR 4 million on time and without audit qualification, most recently under SIDA (2021–2024), Free Press Unlimited (2022), and Internews (2023), and we hold a clean audit from KPMG Türkiye for 2024. Our team of 22 staff and 40 contributors includes vetted Syrian journalists operating in Arabic and Kurdish across multiple governorates, editorial coaches with experience supporting newsrooms in exile, and a safeguarding lead who has developed and implemented our journalist protection framework. We produce multi-platform content in Arabic and Kurdish and have delivered information-integrity programming that directly addresses the disinformation environment in which Syrian journalists operate. Our proposed action will deploy these capabilities across three integrated workstreams: a structured capacity-development programme for 60 journalists and 12 newsroom editors; a Journalist Protection Mechanism providing legal, psychosocial, and digital-security support; and a multi-platform public-awareness campaign on media freedom targeting Syrian audiences inside the country and in diaspora communities. We intend to implement this action in consortium with one EU-eligible co-applicant organisation, whose complementary legal and EU grant management expertise will strengthen the consortium's delivery capacity and administrative compliance.

We respectfully request that the Evaluation Committee consider this concept note for pre-selection to the full application stage. CSIM is committed to full transparency and accountability in the use of EU funds, and we welcome the opportunity to demonstrate in detail how our proposed action will contribute measurably to media freedom and pluralism in Syria. We are available to provide any additional information the contracting authority may require and look forward to the possibility of working in partnership with the European Commission to support Syria's transition toward a rights-based, inclusive future.

Yours sincerely,

[Name of Executive Director / Authorised Representative]
Center for Syrian Independent Media (CSIM)
[Address: Istanbul, Türkiye]
[Email address]
[Telephone number]
[PADOR registration number — to be inserted upon completion]
financial_template_notes: Fixed grant ceiling: The Lot 3 grant is fixed at exactly EUR 675,000 — both the minimum and maximum. The budget must be designed to use this amount in full; there is no flexibility to request more or less. All cost lines must be justified against this ceiling and the action's results framework.

Co-financing rate and source: CSIM is registered in Türkiye, not in Syria, so the default maximum EU co-financing rate of 90% applies, meaning CSIM must source at least EUR 75,000 (10% of EUR 750,000 total eligible costs) from non-EU sources. Verify urgently whether CSIM's operational presence in Syria qualifies it for the 100% co-financing rate under Section 2.1.3 — if so, total eligible costs eq

Eligible cost categories to include: (1) Human resources — CSIM project director (part-time), M&E officer, field coordinators in Gaziantep/Erbil/Qamishli, training facilitators, safeguarding lead, communications officer; (2) Travel and subsistence — field visits, training delivery, community dialogue events; (3) Equipment and supplies — digital-security tools, training materials, video production

Ineligible costs to exclude: Debts and debt-service charges; provisions for losses or debts; interest owed; items already financed by another EU grant; purchases of land or buildings; VAT recoverable by the applicant; exchange-rate losses. Confirm with KPMG Türkiye whether CSIM can recover Turkish VAT on project expenditures.

Budget structure and narrative: Prepare the budget in EUR using the standard EU budget template (Annex B of the full application form). Each cost line must be accompanied by a unit-cost justification (e.g. number of days × daily rate for staff; number of participants × per-diem rate for events).
